notes.fact: Russian, Ukrainian and US delegations opened two days of talks in Abu Dhabi, the first direct round since February, centred on security guarantees.
Meduza says day two lasted under two hours; Kyiv officials said unofficially that Russia refused to discuss ceasefire, territory or energy. Only a large prisoner swap was announced.
A US official said both sides showed private flexibility on territory, while Russia publicly still demands all of Donetsk and Ukraine wants a freeze on the current line.
Kremlin spokesman Peskov said European officials would not take part in the trilateral talks; Lavrov said Europeans could sit in a hotel.
CNN says Putin still makes demands Kyiv has rejected, including control of Donbas and a smaller Ukrainian army; an Atlantic Council analyst urged modest expectations.
Zelensky says Russia's proposed humanitarian operation in Kostiantynivka is a pretext to take the city and push toward Kramatorsk and Sloviansk.
Al Jazeera reports Kyiv claiming the US floated ceding parts of Donbas in return for a NATO path; Zelensky said he refuses to cede territory.
notes.event: US ideas on Donbas and NATO

notes.fact: DTEK said over 600,000 people in Dnipropetrovsk region lost power after a Russian overnight attack; about 250,000 more lost power in Kharkiv region.
Ukrenergo scheduled all-day power cuts across parts of Ukraine, with outages in 12 oblasts; Zelensky says Russia hit energy sites over 310 times since 1 November.
Russia's defence ministry says it will continue strikes on Ukrainian fuel and energy sites it says serve the military; Zelensky says strikes aim to pressure talks.
ISW says Russia fired 310 drones overnight on Nov 3-4, hitting energy sites in Kyiv and several oblasts; Ukraine's energy ministry reported over 20 strikes in 24 hours.
CNN says analysts see Russia hitting power earlier and harder than last year; a UN panel found Russia's strikes on energy last winter were war crimes.
Russia says it shot down 235 Ukrainian drones; Nizhny Novgorod's governor reported significant damage to an industrial site. Trump blames Ukrainian refinery strikes for higher US diesel prices.
notes.claim_by: party:Russia's defence ministry and regional governor

notes.fact: Russia's defence ministry says it downed 1,198 Ukrainian drones overnight over more than 15 regions; Ukraine's air force reported 96 Russian drones overnight to Nov 14.
CNN says a temporary local ceasefire around occupied Oleshky, brokered by Melania Trump, let hundreds of trapped civilians leave; Ukrainian critics call it Kremlin whitewash.
Ukrinform reports Zelensky met mayors on winter preparations; Odesa-region energy strike left nearly 50,000 customers without power; 630 locomotives lost to attacks.
Liveuamap reports G7 foreign ministers backed US-led peace efforts and urged a reciprocal ceasefire and tougher shadow-fleet sanctions; Spain was left out of the EU's negotiating team.
Russia's defence ministry says it hit three cargo ships carrying military goods to Ukraine, near Odesa and in Chornomorsk port.
notes.event: Russian strikes on cargo ships near Odesa

notes.fact: Russia's defence ministry says it struck a dry cargo ship carrying arms for Ukraine southwest of Odesa overnight, per Xinhua.
notes.event: Russian strikes on cargo ships near Odesa

notes.fact: Ukraine's ports authority said the grain ship Golden Leo sank on July 26 after a July 19 Russian missile strike that killed nine crew and a pilot.
Lithuania's defence minister said Poland thwarted a possible provocation on its Kaliningrad border; Lithuania's border is calmer and soldiers there are preventive.
notes.key: claim:lithuania defence minister nato member not fighting
notes.claim_by: official:Lithuania defence minister (NATO member, not fighting)

notes.fact: Lithuania plans to extend heightened Kaliningrad border controls to end-November; up to 100 soldiers assist border guards, with the decision resting on military advice.
Russia's embassy in Belgium warned NATO it could use its whole arsenal if Kaliningrad were isolated; NATO condemned nuclear rhetoric and Vilnius called it psychological pressure.
Business Standard cites Reuters saying NATO aircraft rehearsed cutting Kaliningrad's radio and radar links in August; analysts warn miscalculation could lead to confrontation.
Lithuania's interior minister requested troops on the Kaliningrad border after Latvia-Belarus border incidents and signals Russia may announce mobilisation, saying there was no reason to panic.
Tusk said Poland will not fund US weapons for Ukraine via PURL for now; on Nov 10 Poland and Ukraine agreed joint drone and counter-drone working groups.
Moldova's defence ministry said a drone crossed its airspace for two minutes from Odesa region toward Transnistria during massive Russian attacks on Ukraine.
Agenzia Nova relays Moldovan authorities saying 19 airspace violations were logged in October and six drones exploded on the ground.
Moldova reported two drones on Oct 31; airspace in the north and centre was briefly restricted. Mezha notes Moldova planned to expel a Russian embassy employee after a Oct 23 crash.
Kyiv Independent reports a drone exploded on a Moldovan village outskirts on Sept 30 and a drone resembling Russia's Gerbera type was found on Sept 24.
Iran's Revolutionary Guards say they sent six drones at Bahrain's Riffa helicopter base on Sunday, calling it a reply to US aggression. It is the first direct strike on Bahrain in weeks.
notes.event: IRGC drone strike on Bahrain base

notes.fact: CBS headlined its live blog with Bahrain saying it intercepted Iranian attacks after Tehran claimed it targeted US assets. This is the US side's account of a war the US is fighting.
notes.event: IRGC drone strike on Bahrain base

notes.fact: Arab News, citing Iranian state media via Reuters, says Iran's navy reported a tanker on fire after hitting a mine. It adds that the US military says it has cleared the main routes of mines.
notes.key: claim:iran navy us military disputes mines on main routes
notes.claim_by: party:Iran's navy; US military disputes mines on main routes

notes.fact: NBC says the US military reported new limited 'defensive' strikes. Explosions were heard on Qeshm and Hengam islands and near Bandar Abbas. Page shows no exact date, about three days old.
Trump confirmed on Friday (Nov 6) that the US carried out 'minor strikes' on Iran after Iranian state media reported missiles hitting Qeshm island.
A US official told AP the US struck Iranian targets in Hormuz, saying Iran fired surface-to-air missiles at US assets. AP described the strikes as limited, not a return to full war.
Xinhua, citing two anonymous military sources, says Houthis seized the Kharaz base and nearby heights in Lahj on Sunday, advancing toward Aden. No government or Saudi confirmation is cited.
notes.event: Houthi advance in Lahj toward Aden

notes.fact: Houthi-run Saba says missiles hit a camp holding Saudi officers in Aden. Yemen's army condemned attacks on civilians and did not mention Saudi officers; no casualties were confirmed.
Al Jazeera says the Houthis claim ballistic missiles hit a Saudi coalition command centre in Aden's al-Buraiqa district. Yemen's government says the shelling hits a densely populated area.
The coalition said it intercepted missiles aimed at Taif and Yanbu. The Houthis say Saudi strikes on Sanaa and Hodeida killed 16; this was not independently verified.
notes.event: Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia and Aden

notes.fact: Al Jazeera says Riyadh airport reopened after a two-week closure from Houthi strikes. The Houthis said it remains a military target. Their truce with Saudi Arabia collapsed in July.
notes.event: Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia and Aden

notes.fact: Democracy Now reports Houthi fighters advanced to within about 50 miles of Aden and that Saudi strikes hit Houthi areas. The Houthis say 10 people were killed.
notes.event: Houthi advance in Lahj toward Aden

notes.fact: Hamas confirmed Rafah brigade commander Samir Abu Younis died in an Israeli drone strike in al-Mawasi, Khan Younis, on Saturday. Israel's army and Shin Bet said they targeted a senior commander.
notes.key: claim:israel army and shin bet hamas
notes.event: Strike on Hamas commander in Khan Younis
notes.claim_by: party:Israel's army and Shin Bet; Hamas

notes.fact: Citing Lebanon's Janoubia portal, Azerbaijan's APA says Israeli jets hit at least five south Lebanon towns, drones struck two more areas, and artillery shelled others. Some residents were injured.

Wikipedia's account of the 2026 Lebanon war says Trump declared a US-, Qatar- and Iran-mediated Israel-Hezbollah ceasefire on June 19. Strikes continued the next day. Background only; no recent Hezbollah fire to Israel found.
OCHA counted 397 settler attacks causing casualties or damage between Oct 1 and 26, the highest monthly total since it began recording in 2006. The count excludes the last five days.
Middle East Monitor, citing OCHA, says 62 attacks hit 49 communities from Oct 20 to 26, 38 of them linked to the olive harvest. 57 Palestinians were injured, 23 of them by settlers.

A Palestinian official said Israel's military forced about 1,200 Palestinians from homes in Hebron a day after an attack killed two Israeli soldiers. The Palestinian Authority asked for international pressure on Israel.
Human Rights Watch, citing OCHA, says settlers had killed at least 15 Palestinians in 2026 as of July 24. That puts the year on track to beat the 2023 record of 16.
Wikipedia's page, about five days old, lists a Sept 12 drone attack on Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline blamed on Iraqi militias. Iraqi officials then seized a launcher from one faction.
The Jerusalem Post says Kataib Hezbollah appears to have answered a refinery revelation with a drone strike on the Khor Mor gas field. Date and details are unclear; treat as low confidence.

A suspected car bomb in Jaramana, a Damascus suburb, killed a man and his daughter and seriously hurt his wife. Syria's security forces opened an investigation; no claim of responsibility is reported.

Jordan says its airstrikes in Daraa killed over 20 ISIS members and destroyed a depot. Syria condemned a violation of its sovereignty and said seven people died. Jordan cited an earlier church attack in Jordan.
Syrian media reported Israeli shells near Beit Jinn on Aug 28; Israel offered no confirmation. Syria's foreign minister said in August that security talks with Israel should resume soon.
Sudan's army says it took Iyal Bakhit in West Kordofan, a town it says the RSF used to attack North Kordofan; the claim is unverified.
A Sudan Tribune headline dated 13 Nov says the army and allied forces are advancing toward Al-Khuwai in West Kordofan; no detail in the text I saw.
Two army sources told AFP the army pushed the RSF off the Khartoum–El Obeid highway; RSF drones then hit El Obeid municipal buildings with no casualties reported.
A Sudan Tribune report, citing army and RSF sources, says both sides use imported drones (Pakistani Shahpar, Chinese FH-95); the claims are unverified.
UN News reports that nearly two dozen countries met in Geneva on a ceasefire path; Sudan's government and the RSF were not represented.
A Sudanese civilian anti-war coalition including Abdalla Hamdok urged an immediate humanitarian truce after meeting the African Union's Quintet in Addis Ababa on 12 October.
The US Embassy in Addis Ababa says fighting continues in remote parts of Tigray near the Eritrean border and repeats its do-not-travel advice for Amhara, Tigray and Afar.
notes.event: US embassy alert on northern Ethiopia

notes.fact: Rio Times says it found no independent confirmation of Ethiopian troops inside Eritrea as of 13 November; the two countries have no diplomatic ties.
Ethiopia told the UN Security Council that Eritrean troops advanced up to 60 km into Tigray; Eritrea denies this and the claim is not independently verified.
An unnamed security source told AFP that 5,000 to 8,000 Eritrean troops are in Tigray; Ethiopian drones reportedly struck them near Adigrat (date approximate).
US Africa Command says it carried out an airstrike on al-Shabaab on 12 November near Leego, about 114 km northwest of Mogadishu, coordinated with Somalia's government.
AFRICOM says it struck al-Shabaab on 5 November near Jamaame, about 40 km northeast of Kismayo, and gave no unit details.
AFRICOM lists airstrikes on al-Shabaab on 17, 19 and 21 October, including one near Dhooble Airport, about 180 km northwest of Kismayo.
AFP reports local sources say armed men killed at least 37 civilians on 12 November near Tera in Tillaberi; the attackers are unidentified.
Pakistani outlet 24NewsHD carried the AFP report: at least 37 civilians killed in a Niger ambush near the Burkina Faso and Mali borders, per local sources.
Bangladesh's New Age, carrying AFP, says a Tera resident confirmed 37 dead including women and children, and one more victim died a day later.
1 Nation Media says JNIM claimed an attack that week on an escorted tanker convoy east of Bamako; the casualty toll was unclear and Malian authorities gave no detailed account.
Modern Diplomacy says JNIM has destroyed over 300 tankers since September 2025, yet over 1,000 reached the capital by July 2026 under Russian and Turkish drone cover.
Human Rights Watch says M23 left Uvira in January 2026 but holds positions north of the city, and fighting with Congolese forces and Wazalendo continues.
Taiwan's defence ministry says it tracked 10 Chinese military aircraft, 8 navy ships and 3 official ships in 24 hours; 4 aircraft crossed the median line.
A UAE outlet repeats Taiwan's tally of 10 aircraft and 8 warships, adding that Taiwan has logged 184 aircraft and 141 ships so far in November.
Taiwan's defence ministry says 30 Chinese military aircraft were tracked in one day, 23 of them crossing the median line; this is above the 15-aircraft easing threshold.
Taiwan's defence ministry reported one PLA aircraft, eight PLA Navy ships and three Chinese official ships near the island on Sunday, a quieter air count than on Nov 13.
Taiwan's defence ministry said it tracked 49 Chinese military aircraft and 12 ships in 24 hours, with 31 aircraft crossing the median line.
Taiwan Ministry of National Defense data showed Chinese aircraft were tracked 232 times and ships 363 times during October 2026.
Taiwan's coast guard said a Chinese vessel entered restricted waters near Pratas, the 13th such intrusion this year; China announced a patrol east of Taiwan the same day.
notes.event: Chinese coast guard near Pratas and east of Taiwan

notes.fact: President Lai warned of Chinese interference in the Nov 28 local elections; China's Taiwan Affairs Office rejected the claims as invented for electoral gain, citing Reuters.
Reuters reports DPP candidate Puma Shen is within reach of the KMT's Chiang Wan-an in the Taipei mayoral race, which Shen says is a test of democracy against Chinese pressure.

The Wire China commentary says the Chinese coast guard has expanded patrols off Taiwan's east coast since June and radios foreign ships heading to Taiwanese ports; this is analysis, not an official claim.
Taiwan's National Security Bureau said government networks faced about 2.58 million intrusion attempts a day as of September, and linked the rise possibly to election interference.
Four Chinese coast guard ships entered Japanese-claimed waters off the Senkakus for about two hours, the first such entry since Oct 10, Japan Coast Guard said.
Tokyo said PM Takaichi will visit the Philippines and China from Nov 16 to 19 for ASEAN-related meetings and the APEC summit, her first China trip as PM.
Kyodo, via a South Korean outlet, reports a formal Xi-Takaichi meeting at APEC appears to have fallen through; Japan may be the only major leader without talks with Xi.
Turkish outlet Anadolu-linked site, citing Kyodo, says China wants Takaichi to retract her Taiwan remarks before bilateral talks can proceed.
Bloomberg reports Japan is working to secure at least a customary handshake from Xi, and calls ties among the lowest since normalisation in 1972.
South Korea's defence ministry says North Korea fired multiple missiles toward the sea off its east coast from Sondok, its fourth launch in a month, NBC reports.
US Pacific Command said the Nov 4 launches posed no immediate threat to US personnel, territory or allies; South Korea's JCS said it kept a robust combined posture with the US.
Pakistani and Afghan border forces traded fire at several points; Torkham closed for about five hours, and one civilian died in mortar shelling near Angoor Adda.
Afghanistan International reported that Pakistan's air operation 'Ghazab lil Haq' had cut intensity by late March, and Afghan analysts said Pakistan struck Kabul earlier in 2026.
NPR reported the Torkham border had been shut since mid-October 2025 with no end in sight, stranding trucks and straining medicine supplies.
The Manila Times reported a Chinese coast guard boat approached the BRP Sierra Madre and a Filipino sailor was struck on the head; the ship later left, per SeaLight.
AP reports gangs fired on an armoured vehicle in Croix-des-Bouquets on Oct 18, leaving four Salvadoran soldiers unaccounted for; no group claimed it.
GSF chief Jack Christofides told the UN that attacks on the force have increased, while saying early signs of reduced gang control are appearing in some areas.
Al Jazeera says four Salvadoran aviation technicians were kidnapped on Oct 18 and El Salvador responded by sending up to 2,000 troops; no release reported in this article.
notes.event: Missing Salvadoran troops and El Salvador surge

notes.fact: G7 foreign ministers meeting in Paris backed the Gang Suppression Force; Amnesty International asked El Salvador and Haiti to publish the deployment agreement and rules on use of force.
notes.event: G7 backs GSF; Salvadoran buildup scrutiny

notes.fact: The UN Security Council extended the Gang Suppression Force to March 31, 2027; China, Russia and Pakistan abstained, and the force is at about 30% of intended size.
The GSF says it ran operations in Tabarre on Oct 5 and Cité Soleil on Oct 6, with arrests, weapons seizures and several gang members killed.
notes.event: GSF operations in Tabarre and Cité Soleil

notes.fact: The UN says the council voted 12-0 with 3 abstentions for resolution 2829; the US cited progress, while China and Russia questioned the approach.
The Colombian army says four soldiers died and five were hurt when about 20 drone-dropped explosives hit troops at Barco La Silla, Tibú, on Nov 12.
President De la Espriella confirmed the deaths on X and said security and intelligence work would be reinforced; the army attributes the attack preliminarily to the ELN.
Semana reports the area where soldiers died is contested by the ELN and a FARC dissident faction led by alias Calarcá; it was still checking who was behind it.
Spanish outlet El Demócrata, citing Caracol Radio, says the attack came during a 21-month military offensive in Catatumbo against the ELN and FARC dissidents.
Democracy Now, citing the New York Times and four US officials, says the US gave Venezuela drones and intelligence for a deadly strike on the ELN on Oct 30.
The Inquirer reports the US military and other agencies conduct counter-drug operations in Colombia, including joint actions with Colombian forces; details were not given.
Government data shown at Sheinbaum's morning briefing counted 1,156 homicides in Sinaloa in the first 10 months of 2026, 18.8% fewer than the same period last year.
Mexico News Daily reported Sinaloa violence moving south to Mazatlán, where homicides in August exceeded those in Culiacán despite 1,000 marines being sent.
Crisis Group says Sheinbaum is trying to deter US military action in Mexico; Washington indicted Sinaloa politicians, and Mexican forces killed CJNG leader El Mencho.
notes.event: US pressure on Mexico over cartels

notes.fact: US Southern Command says it killed five people on an alleged drug boat in the eastern Pacific on Oct 27, offering no public evidence of drugs aboard.
Al Jazeera, citing the WOLA tracker, puts the toll at about 243 dead since September 2025 and quotes the analyst saying it was the sixth lethal strike in four months.
InSight Crime's timeline, updated Nov 6, lists Oct 27 as the latest lethal strike, after one on Oct 4; the Aug 23 strike ended a gap of over two months.
Rubio told the New York Times the US seeks a 'presence agreement' so US troops can operate jointly with Venezuela, per a secondary outlet; no text or sites are public.
EFE reports Noboa gave the armed forces 5,570 assault rifles and 20 light machine guns on Nov 10, part of $24.5 million in equipment.
Al Jazeera reports Trump said he would 'certainly consider' military force against Cuba and wants to 'get Cuba done' before leaving office in 2029.
notes.event: Trump says he would consider force against Cuba

notes.fact: HNGN says Trump added the US is 'talking to Cuba' without naming who; Cuban officials have not described talks, and analysts see more sanctions as likelier than force.
notes.event: Trump says he would consider force against Cuba

notes.fact: Wikipedia's running entry says the US has blocked tankers bound for Cuba since February and threatened tariffs on suppliers; Cuba reported in May that it had run out of oil.

The Wall Street Journal reports suspected Iranian hackers locked operators out of small-town Midwest water-station controls, breached two Texas-bound tankers and overheated hundreds of European store fridges since summer.
notes.event: WSJ report on Iran-linked infrastructure hacking

notes.fact: French judicial authorities attribute last month's attack on refrigeration systems at hundreds of French stores to Iran's Revolutionary Guards, naming three Iranians and issuing international arrest warrants, per a report relaying the WSJ.
notes.event: France blames IRGC for fridge attacks

notes.fact: RTÉ reports that on Monday Nov 2 refrigeration systems in at least eight European countries were hit, including 13 SuperValu stores in Ireland, with some set as high as 50C.
notes.event: Irish report on European fridge hacks

notes.fact: CISA, FBI, HHS, USDA and DOT issued a joint fact sheet warning that industrial refrigeration and cold-chain monitoring systems are being targeted, with steps such as removing devices from the internet and changing default passwords.
notes.key: claim:cisa fbi us not a direct party to this european hacking
notes.claim_by: official:CISA/FBI (US government; not a direct party to this European hacking)

notes.fact: TechCrunch says the US has not formally named a culprit, though researchers and reportedly US officials suspect Iran; affected units included Danfoss remote-control models whose maker had stopped security updates.

Science Times reports water-system intrusions across at least 12 US states; Iran-linked hackers are leading suspects, but no formal attribution, with localized rather than widespread service problems.

A secondary site says reports dated Nov 2-10 describe continued targeting of internet-exposed Rockwell/Allen-Bradley controllers at US water facilities; single low-authority source, not confirmed by an agency page seen.
CISA, FBI, NSA and EPA updated advisory AA26-097A on July 23, saying Iran-affiliated actors altered controller logic at US water utilities, in one case disabling shutdown and alarm functions.
CSIS reports hackers hit more than 30 Minnesota water systems in July; in Georgia a pump station shutdown cut pressure and led to a boil-water advisory, with no illnesses reported.
Microsoft 365 suffered a widespread outage on Nov 12-13; Microsoft said it saw no evidence of malicious activity and traced it to overwhelmed servers after a network configuration change.

A Substack roundup says the FAA halted flights nationwide for about five hours on Nov 13 after communications failures, with officials citing aging equipment; unverified blog, no cyber evidence reported.
Dutch police detained a man (49) and woman (41) on Nov 12 over rail sabotage on Sept 15, suspected of advising on how to cause disruption; both were released after questioning.
The Hacker News reports the DOJ seized and restrained over $1.2 billion in crypto stolen by North Korea-linked TraderTraitor after the Binance hack.
notes.key: claim:us doj not a party to korean standoff
notes.event: US action over North Korea crypto theft
notes.claim_by: official:US DOJ (not a party to the Korean standoff)

notes.fact: The Hacker News reports hackers exploited N-central flaws to infect 21 servers, and N-able is investigating new claims of exploits against patched on-premise versions in the Americas, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
CISA's page lists five Siemens industrial-control advisories on Nov 12 (including building automation, Desigo and Gridscale products) and KEV additions on Nov 13.

Defense One reports that President Trump nominated Palantir security chief Michael LoSapio to lead CISA on Monday Nov 9; acting director Nick Andersen circulated an internal risk-assessment framework on Nov 5.
CISA launched its November Critical Infrastructure Security and Resilience Month, urging operators to map dependencies, prioritise risks and plan recovery, with attention to operational technology.

UNM Health said clinical operations were fully functional after the Oct 26 cyberattack that caused ambulance diversions and cancelled appointments, and told the public not to engage with groups claiming it.
A Centrum Balticum briefing says Taiwan convicted the Hong Tai 58 captain on his own conduct without proving a state sponsor, while a prosecutor declined to charge the Hai Hong Gong 66 captain.
A cable-incident log says that by mid-2026 several North Sea and Baltic governments grew more confident that most recent breaks were accidents; anchor-drag cases are hard to prove deliberate.
A secondary analysis says the Iran war froze Persian Gulf cable projects and repairs, and Tehran threatened fees on cables under the Strait of Hormuz; not independently checked.
notes.event: Gulf cable risk during Iran war

notes.fact: An aggregator, citing Free Malaysia Today, says Malaysia's health ministry suffered a cybersecurity breach but patient services were not affected.
notes.hotspot: cyber: new: Malaysia health ministry breach
